speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. You've reported persistent vomiting and chest pain; please describe exactly where the pain is located, how severe it is on a scale of 0 to 10, and what specific symptoms accompany the vomiting, such as blood, fever, or shortness of breath.

REQUEST TEST: ECG

speaker: Doctor
text: The ECG results show normal readings. Given your persistent vomiting and chest pain, are you experiencing any difficulty swallowing, regurgitation of undigested food, or a sensation of food getting stuck in your chest?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture)

The clinical picture of forceful vomiting after alcohol consumption followed by sudden chest pain and coughing, despite a normal ECG, is highly specific for an esophageal tear. I request an emergent CT scan of the chest with IV contrast to confirm the diagnosis.

REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_With_Contrast
